title: Dropbox sync folder
whyItMatters: Everything the person keeps in Dropbox is also on this disk, readable without any password. The folder names alone show their work and private life.
source: Arch Wiki, Dropbox: the desktop client syncs to ~/Dropbox by default and keeps its state in ~/.dropbox: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Dropbox
notes: Dropbox asks for the sync location during setup and it can be changed later, so this is the default only. Business accounts may use a named folder instead. The account and folder list live in ~/.dropbox, which this rule does not count.

cleanup.exportFirst: Check that every file you need is uploaded to your Dropbox account; files that never synced are deleted with the local folder.
cleanup.signOut: Sign in at dropbox.com, open Settings > Security, find this computer under Devices and click Unlink.
steps: Quit the Dropbox desktop app from its tray icon.
Uninstall the Dropbox app from the App Center or from Discover if you no longer need it.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes the local copies of everything in Dropbox, plus anything that never finished syncing. The files stay in the Dropbox account.
cleanup.source: Dropbox Help, View your devices and log out remotely: https://help.dropbox.com/security/device-list-remote-sign-out
